# datahub_page_module (Resource)

**DataHub ✅ | DataHub Cloud ✅**

Creates and manages a DataHub page module -- one widget on a page laid out by `datahub_page_template`.

Modules are separate resources rather than blocks inside a template because DataHub addresses them independently and one module can appear on several templates. Reference a module's `urn` from a template's `rows` and Terraform orders the two correctly with no `depends_on`.

## Naming

`page_module_id` becomes the URN suffix (`urn:li:dataHubPageModule:<page_module_id>`) and the provider always sends it. DataHub mints a random UUID when a module is created without an explicit URN, which is what the DataHub UI does -- so a module created in the UI has a UUID URN, while one created here is stable and predictable across a destroy and re-apply. That stability is what lets a page survive a rebuild.

## Module types

`type` is passed to DataHub unvalidated by the provider, deliberately: DataHub's module catalogue grows between releases (22 types in Cloud v2.0.3, 30 in v2.1.0), and a list compiled into the provider would make each new type unusable until the provider shipped a release. An unrecognised type is rejected by the server.

Types taking no parameters include `DOMAINS`, `DATA_PRODUCTS`, `OWNED_ASSETS`, `ASSETS` and `PLATFORMS`. The five that take parameters each have a matching block under `params`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A rich-text module for a welcome banner.
resource "datahub_page_module" "welcome" {
  page_module_id = "welcome-banner"
  name           = "Welcome"
  type           = "RICH_TEXT"

  params = {
    rich_text = {
      content = "Welcome to the data catalog. Start with the Finance domain below."
    }
  }
}

# A link module pointing at an internal runbook.
resource "datahub_page_module" "runbook" {
  page_module_id = "data-runbook"
  name           = "Data platform runbook"
  type           = "LINK"

  params = {
    link = {
      link_url    = "https://example.internal/data-runbook"
      description = "On-call procedures and escalation paths"
    }
  }
}

# Many module types need no parameters at all -- they render a standard view.
resource "datahub_page_module" "domains" {
  page_module_id = "browse-domains"
  name           = "Domains"
  type           = "DOMAINS"
}

# A hierarchy module rooted on specific domains. Referencing the domain
# resource's urn rather than hardcoding a string gives Terraform the dependency
# edge, so the domain is created before the module that points at it.
resource "datahub_page_module" "finance_tree" {
  page_module_id = "finance-hierarchy"
  name           = "Finance hierarchy"
  type           = "HIERARCHY"

  params = {
    hierarchy_view = {
      asset_urns            = [datahub_domain.finance.urn]
      show_related_entities = true
    }
  }
}

resource "datahub_domain" "finance" {
  domain_id = "finance"
  name      = "Finance"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name shown on the module.
- `page_module_id` (String) Identifier forming the URN suffix. Changing this replaces the module, because the URN is derived from it.
- `type` (String) Module type, e.g. `LINK`, `RICH_TEXT`, `DOMAINS`, `ASSET_COLLECTION`, `HIERARCHY`. Validated by DataHub, not by the provider.

### Optional

- `params` (Attributes) Type-specific configuration. Supply exactly the block matching `type`; most module types need none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params))
- `scope` (String) Visibility scope. Only `GLOBAL` is supported; `PERSONAL` modules are per-user preferences and out of scope for this provider.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Terraform identifier. Same value as `page_module_id`.
- `urn` (String) Full DataHub URN, `urn:li:dataHubPageModule:<page_module_id>`.

<a id="nestedatt--params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params`

Optional:

- `agent_card` (Attributes) For `type = "AGENT_CARD"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--agent_card))
- `asset_collection` (Attributes) For `type = "ASSET_COLLECTION"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--asset_collection))
- `hierarchy_view` (Attributes) For `type = "HIERARCHY"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--hierarchy_view))
- `link` (Attributes) For `type = "LINK"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--link))
- `rich_text` (Attributes) For `type = "RICH_TEXT"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--rich_text))

<a id="nestedatt--params--agent_card"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.agent_card`

Optional:

- `agent_urn` (String) URN of the agent to surface.
- `display_mode` (String) Presentation mode for the card.


<a id="nestedatt--params--asset_collection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.asset_collection`

Optional:

- `asset_urns` (List of String) URNs of the assets to show.
- `dynamic_filter_json` (String) Raw DataHub filter JSON selecting assets dynamically.


<a id="nestedatt--params--hierarchy_view"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.hierarchy_view`

Optional:

- `asset_urns` (List of String) Root URNs of the hierarchy, e.g. domain or glossary node URNs.
- `related_entities_filter_json` (String) Raw DataHub filter JSON narrowing the related entities.
- `show_related_entities` (Boolean) Whether to include related entities beneath each root.


<a id="nestedatt--params--link"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.link`

Optional:

- `description` (String) Optional descriptive text.
- `image_url` (String) Optional image shown on the card.
- `link_url` (String) Target URL.


<a id="nestedatt--params--rich_text"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.rich_text`

Optional:

- `content` (String) Module body content.
